plainDefinition: Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate: A number calculated from a blood test that shows how well your kidney filters are cleaning waste, scaled for an average adult body size (100 is top health, around 60-90 is mild, under 60 shows CKD).
A natural waste product produced by your muscles during everyday movement. Healthy kidneys filter it out into urine. If kidneys filter slower, creatinine levels in the blood rise.
Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratio: A simple urine test that checks for tiny amounts of a protein called albumin in your urine. Healthy kidneys keep protein in the blood; leaks show kidney strain.
The microscopic filtering unit inside your kidney. Each kidney has around one million nephrons quietly cleaning your blood.
The top number on a blood pressure reading. It measures the pressure in your blood vessels when your heart beats and pumps blood.
The bottom number on a blood pressure reading. It measures the resting pressure in your blood vessels between heartbeats.
Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drug. A family of painkillers (such as ibuprofen and naproxen) that can reduce blood flow to kidney filters.
A qualified healthcare professional who translates nutritional science into practical, safe eating guidance for medical conditions.
